ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: The Liking Gap / The Old Guitarist / Mama Cax

fullPassage:
Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I'm a guidance counselor at the local college. I also have a social media channel where I give advice to young students like you. Today I'd like to talk to you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you ever asked yourself whether you made a good impression on someone you just met? In fact, most people believe they make a worse impression than they actually do. Researchers performed an experiment where students were paired up for five-minute ice breaking conversations. They were then asked to rate how much they liked their partners. Additionally, researchers asked participants if they thought their partners liked them. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were pessimistic, which were opposite to the real responses. It turns out that participants do not make bad impressions but make better impressions than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception or the mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and what others actually think of us. How is this helpful for you? We often underestimate ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential. Don't worry about the impression you think you make on people; chances are you can be confident that the impression you make is just fine.
The second point I want to make today is about thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category and often blame their weaknesses or failures on their personality type. For example, they may say they can't do something because they aren't that kind of person. However, personality categorizations are neither absolute nor permanent.
Try to remember yourself from ten years ago. Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope to become when you grow up? Do you feel the same way now? What will your answers be 10 years from now? I bet you don't know. Just like your likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you. If you choose to behave differently and make needed changes, your personality will also change. People are predictable and consistent over time only because they choose to be, so don't limit yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person you want to become today.
Hello, everyone! Thank you for your warm welcome. It's good to be back home, but I'm visiting you today not to perform but to talk to you about my life as a musician. Last year, after 20 years of hard work, I finally signed my first record company contract. I'd like to tell you a hopeful story and give some insight into the hard work that I had to put in.
Look at this picture of Picasso's The Old Guitarist behind me. My grandfather was a classical guitarist, and on my 13th birthday, he gave me this picture and a new guitar. After he passed away, I hung it up in my room as a reminder of his love for music.
I wasn't a musical genius, but I was better than most. I was popular at school festivals, and I thought I was born to be a musician. But things were far from easy. In college, I had to compete with classmates who were definitely more capable than I was. I don't even remember how many contests I went to and came up short. I kept failing no matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every disappointment made me lose hope more and more. I wanted to give up.
The funny thing was whenever anyone asked me to play a song for them, I would be so happy. Although my dream was to record an album, the reality was I probably wouldn't make it. Then one day, I looked at the picture of The Old Guitarist on my wall. I suddenly remembered what my grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a tiny fraction of the thousands of artworks he created during his lifetime are recognized by the public. Then I thought of my grandfather and how he loved playing, practicing his art his entire life, even without fame. I realized the only way to become an old guitarist like him was to keep playing.
The happy ending to this story is that after having sent my recordings to countless producers, I finally found one who was eager to work with me. One thing led to another, and I finally signed a record deal. Opportunities only come to those who are prepared. I had spent years performing on unknown streets and writing songs no one recognized. The difficulties I faced were part of my journey. If you love something, keep trying. Someday an opportunity may come knocking at your door, and you have to be ready to welcome it.
During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman with a brightly decorated prosthetic leg proudly walked the runway at a major fashion show. She was Mama Cax, a model and influencer.
Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was depressed and struggled to accept her new body. However, with the support of her family and friends, Cax learned to love it. One day when she was 26, Cax posted a picture on social media showing her leg. "I didn't think it could help anyone," she said in an interview, "But after receiving messages of support, I realized my story could inspire others." After receiving support from others, she began to use social media to share more about her life and to inspire others. She proudly posted pictures of herself wearing stylish prosthetic covers and spoke out about body positivity and fashion. In 2016, she became the first model for the #RunwayForAll campaign. In 2018, she appeared on the cover of major fashion magazines.
When asked, "How did you come to embrace yourself?" she replied, "The truth is, like many people, I'm still on my journey to self-love. There are many barriers ahead." In addition to modeling, Cax showed her ability to overcome physical barriers by swimming, playing basketball, and mountain climbing. She even finished the New York City Marathon in a wheelchair.
Sadly, Mama Cax's journey was cut short in 2019. Although she is no longer with us, her journey will remain in our hearts, inspiring us to overcome limitations and find our own paths to success and happiness.

questions.passage: Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I'm a guidance (A)[counselor / chancellor] at the local college. I also have a social media channel where I give advice to young students like you. Have you ever asked yourself whether you made a good (B)[impression / expression] on someone you just met? In fact, most people believe they make a worse impression than they actually do. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were (C)[pessimistic / optimistic], which were opposite to the real responses.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 안녕하세요, 저는 Laura Thompson이고 지역 대학의 상담사(counselor)입니다. 처음 만난 사람에게 좋은 인상(impression)을 주었는지 자문해 본 적이 있나요? 대부분의 추정은 비관적(pessimistic)이었습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① counselor–impression–pessimistic: 문맥 모두 적합
❌ ② chancellor는 guidance와 부적합
❌ ③ expression은 make a good과 부적합
❌ ④ 둘 다 오류
det.tip: counselor(상담사) vs chancellor(총장) / impression(인상) vs expression(표현)

questions.passage: I wasn't a musical (A)[genius / amateur], but I was better than most. I was popular at school festivals, and I thought I was born to be a musician. But things were (B)[far from / close to] easy. In college, I had to (C)[compete / cooperate] with classmates who were definitely more capable than I was. I don't even remember how many contests I went to and came up short.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 음악 천재(genius)는 아니었지만 나았습니다. 상황은 전혀(far from) 쉽지 않았습니다. 동급생들과 경쟁(compete)해야 했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ genius–far from–compete: 모두 적합
❌ ① cooperate는 경쟁 상황과 부적합
❌ ② amateur는 better than most와 모순
❌ ④ cooperate+amateur 둘 다 오류
det.tip: far from + 형용사 = 전혀 ~하지 않은 / compete ↔ cooperate

questions.passage: During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman with a brightly decorated (A)[prosthetic / synthetic] leg proudly walked the runway at a major fashion show. She was Mama Cax, a model and influencer. Cax was (B)[diagnosed / dismissed] with cancer at age 14 and lost her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was (C)[depressed / impressed] and struggled to accept her new body. However, with the support of her family and friends, Cax learned to love it.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 의족(prosthetic) 다리를 한 여성이 런웨이를 걸었습니다. Cax는 14세에 암 진단(diagnosed)을 받았습니다. 처음에 우울(depressed)했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① prosthetic–diagnosed–depressed: 모두 적합
❌ ② synthetic은 인공 다리에 부적합, impressed는 struggled와 모순
❌ ③ dismissed는 with cancer와 부적합
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: prosthetic(의족) vs synthetic(합성의) / diagnosed with ↔ dismissed

questions.passage: In fact, most people believe they make a ①<u>worse</u> impression than they actually do. Researchers performed an experiment where students were ②<u>paired up</u> for five-minute ice breaking conversations. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were ③<u>pessimistic</u>, which were opposite to the real responses. It turns out that participants do not make bad impressions but make ④<u>inferior</u> impressions than they think.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①나쁜 인상을 준다고 믿습니다. ②짝지어 대화하게 했습니다. ③비관적이었습니다. 나쁜 인상이 아니라 더 나은(better) 인상을 줍니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ inferior → better: not bad but ___이므로 긍정적 단어 필요
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: not A but B: B는 A의 반대 / inferior ↔ superior, better ↔ worse

questions.passage: Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category and often ①<u>blame</u> their weaknesses on their personality type. However, personality categorizations are neither ②<u>absolute</u> nor permanent. If you choose to behave ③<u>identically</u> and make needed changes, your personality will also change. People are ④<u>predictable</u> and consistent over time only because they choose to be.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 약점을 성격 탓으로 ①돌립니다. 성격 분류는 ②절대적이지 않습니다. ③다르게(differently) 행동하면 성격도 바뀝니다. ④예측 가능합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ identically → differently: 변화를 만들려면 다르게 행동해야 함
❌ ①②④: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: identically(동일하게) ↔ differently(다르게)

questions.passage: Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was ①<u>depressed</u> and struggled to accept her new body. She ②<u>proudly</u> posted pictures of herself wearing stylish prosthetic covers and spoke out about body positivity. In addition to modeling, Cax showed her ability to ③<u>overcome</u> physical barriers by swimming, playing basketball, and mountain climbing. Sadly, Mama Cax's journey was ④<u>extended</u> in 2019.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①우울했습니다. ②자랑스럽게 사진을 올렸습니다. ③장벽을 극복했습니다. 슬프게도 여정은 2019년에 중단(cut short)되었습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ extended → cut short: Sadly가 단서 — 연장이 아니라 중단
❌ ①②③: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: extended(연장) ↔ cut short(중단) / Sadly가 부정적 결과 암시

questions.passage: Have you ever asked yourself whether you made a good impression on someone you just met? In fact, most people believe they make a worse impression than they actually do. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were pessimistic, which were opposite to the real responses. It turns out that participants make better impressions than they think. The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception or the __________ between how we perceive ourselves and what others actually think of us.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 연구자들은 인식의 차이 또는 불일치(mismatch)를 '호감 격차'라고 이름 붙였습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ mismatch: or 병렬 → difference와 유사
❌ ① perception: 앞에 이미 나옴
❌ ② impression: 의미 부적합
❌ ③ assumption: 의미 부적합
det.tip: A or B 병렬: B는 A와 유사 / difference ≈ mismatch

questions.passage: Although my dream was to record an album, the reality was I probably wouldn't make it. Then one day, I looked at the picture of The Old Guitarist on my wall. I suddenly remembered what my grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a tiny __________ of the thousands of artworks he created during his lifetime are recognized by the public. questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 피카소의 수천 점 중 극히 일부(fraction)만 대중에게 인정받습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ fraction: tiny fraction = 극히 일부
❌ ① majority: tiny와 모순
❌ ② portion: 가능하지만 tiny fraction이 관용적
❌ ④ collection: 의미 부적합
det.tip: a tiny fraction of = 극히 일부

questions.passage: Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category. However, personality categorizations are neither absolute nor permanent. Just like your likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you. If you choose to behave differently and make needed changes, your personality will also change. People are predictable and __________ over time only because they choose to be, so don't limit yourself to a certain type.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 예측 가능하고 일관된(consistent) 이유는 스스로 그렇게 선택하기 때문입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ consistent: and 병렬 → predictable과 유사
❌ ①②④: 전부 '변한다'는 의미 → predictable과 반대
det.tip: A and B 병렬: B는 A와 유사 / predictable ≈ consistent

questions.passage: How is this helpful for you? We often <u>underestimate</u> ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 underestimate와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 스스로를 과소평가(underestimate)합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② undervalue: 동의어
❌ ① overvalue: 반의어
❌ ③ exaggerate: 과장하다
❌ ④ calculate: 계산하다
det.tip: underestimate = undervalue = 과소평가하다

questions.passage: When asked, "How did you come to <u>embrace</u> yourself?" she replied, "The truth is, like many people, I'm still on my journey to self-love. There are many barriers ahead."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 embrace와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 어떻게 자기 자신을 받아들이게(embrace) 됐나요?
det.analysis:
✅ ① accept: embrace = accept
❌ ② reject: 반의어
❌ ③ ignore: 무시하다
❌ ④ abandon: 버리다
det.tip: embrace = accept = 받아들이다 (비유적)

questions.passage: People are predictable and consistent over time only because they choose to be, so don't limit yourself to a certain type. Start <u>crafting</u> the person you want to become today.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 crafting과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 되고 싶은 사람을 만들어(crafting) 나가세요.
det.analysis:
✅ ② create: crafting = 만들다
❌ ① perform: 수행하다
❌ ③ collect: 수집하다
❌ ④ display: 전시하다
det.tip: craft = 공들여 만들다

questions.passage: Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were <u>pessimistic</u>, which were opposite to the real responses. It turns out that participants do not make bad impressions but make better impressions than they think.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 pessimistic과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 추정은 비관적(pessimistic)이었습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① optimistic: 정확한 반의어
❌ ② skeptical: 회의적 — 반의어 아님
❌ ③ realistic: -istic 혼동
❌ ④ enthusiastic: 긍정적이지만 반의어 아님
det.tip: pessimistic ↔ optimistic

questions.passage: Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category. However, personality categorizations are neither absolute nor <u>permanent</u>. Just like your likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 permanent와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 성격 분류는 영구적(permanent)이지 않습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ temporary: 정확한 반의어
❌ ① eternal: 동의어 — 함정
❌ ② inevitable: 무관
❌ ③ definite: absolute와 유사 — 혼동
det.tip: permanent ↔ temporary / eternal은 동의어 함정

questions.passage:
(A) I don't even remember how many contests I went to and came up <u>short</u>. I kept failing no matter how hard I tried.

(B) Sadly, Mama Cax's journey was cut <u>short</u> in 2019. Although she is no longer with us, her journey will remain in our hearts.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 short의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 대회에서 실패했습니다(came up short). (B) 여정이 중단되었습니다(cut short).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 부족한–중단된: come up short = 실패, cut short = 중단
❌ ① 물리적 의미
❌ ② 부적합
❌ ④ (A)(B) 의미 뒤바뀜
det.tip: come up short = 실패하다 / cut short = 중단하다

❌ ② synthetic: 합성의

❌ ④ diagnostic: 진단의
